frozen_rule: The target prompt states requirements and observable constraints, never the organising mechanism.

candidates.title: Shared worker permits
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python module that grants at most N simultaneous permits to named workers. A worker may crash and later return. Other workers must eventually regain abandoned capacity. The public API must support request, renew, release, and inspect operations, use only the standard library, and produce deterministic results under a supplied clock.
candidates.hidden_structure: expiring leases with fencing generations
candidates.admission_rationale: Specifies safety, recovery, API, and determinism but not how abandoned capacity is detected or stale holders are excluded.
candidates.human_analogy: Library loans: a borrower has a dated claim that can be renewed; after the due date the copy can circulate again, and an old receipt cannot reclaim it.

candidates.title: Resumable multi-step migration
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python migration runner for a sequence of named steps. Re-running after interruption must not repeat completed external effects, must continue from the earliest unfinished work, and must expose an inspectable record explaining the next action. Steps can fail before or after reporting their effect. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: durable intent/effect checkpoint protocol
candidates.admission_rationale: States interruption and observability requirements without prescribing how intent and completion are represented.
candidates.human_analogy: A mountain expedition signs huts on arrival and carries the next route card; after rescue, the register shows the last confirmed hut rather than relying on memory.

candidates.title: Explainable configuration choice
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python resolver that chooses one value from defaults, organization settings, project settings, and command-line input. Some values may be explicitly unset. The result must include both the chosen value and a concise explanation of which inputs mattered. Adding a new input source must not require rewriting every pairwise case. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: ordered provenance-bearing candidates folded by precedence
candidates.admission_rationale: Names sources and desired explanation but withholds the compositional representation and resolution mechanism.
candidates.human_analogy: An archaeological layer stack: the uppermost applicable layer determines what is visible, while the excavation log preserves why lower layers did not.

candidates.title: Duplicate-safe command handling
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python command handler that may receive the same command many times and may restart between calls. For a given command identity, the external effect must occur at most once and every caller must receive the same recorded result. Distinct commands with identical payloads remain distinct. Provide an in-memory storage interface and use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: idempotency-key result journal
candidates.admission_rationale: Defines identity and replay semantics but does not tell the implementation what durable fact to store.
candidates.human_analogy: A coat-check desk returns the same coat for the same numbered ticket; identical coats with different tickets remain separate obligations.

candidates.title: Stable rollout assignment
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python function that assigns users to rollout cohorts for named features. Assignments must be deterministic across processes, close to a requested percentage, independently adjustable per feature, and minimally disturbed when a percentage changes slightly. Python hash randomization must not affect results. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: stable digest mapped onto a fixed numeric ring
candidates.admission_rationale: States stability and minimal movement but withholds the coordinate system used to achieve them.
candidates.human_analogy: Permanent seats in a circular stadium: opening one more section admits nearby ticket numbers without reseating everyone already inside.

candidates.title: Selective rebuild planner
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python planner for named artifacts with declared input artifacts. Given changed artifacts, return a valid rebuild order containing every affected artifact and no unaffected artifact. Reject dependency cycles with a useful explanation. The same graph and changes must always produce the same order. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: reverse dependency closure followed by stable topological order
candidates.admission_rationale: Defines observable affectedness, ordering, cycle behavior, and determinism without naming graph algorithms.
candidates.human_analogy: A watershed map traced upstream from polluted outlets identifies every tributary that can carry contamination, then cleanup proceeds from springs toward the outlet.

candidates.title: Burst-tolerant admission
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python admission controller that allows an average of R operations per second, permits short bursts up to B, never invents capacity while idle beyond B, and returns the exact wait time when an operation cannot proceed. It must be deterministic under a supplied monotonic clock and use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: continuously refilled bounded credit reservoir
candidates.admission_rationale: States rate and burst invariants but not the state representation or update equation.
candidates.human_analogy: A cistern fills at a steady trickle, can release water quickly, never holds more than its walls allow, and predicts delay from the missing volume.

candidates.title: Fresh-enough reads during refresh
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python cache that distinguishes usable, refresh-needed, and unusable entries. One caller should be elected to refresh while concurrent callers may receive a still-usable old value; after a hard deadline no old value may be returned. Failures during refresh must leave inspectable state. Use a supplied clock and only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: entry state machine with soft and hard deadlines plus single refresh claim
candidates.admission_rationale: Defines states behaviorally and asks for election but does not reveal transition representation or coordination structure.
candidates.human_analogy: A restaurant keeps serving yesterday’s printed menu while one editor prepares today’s edition, but destroys it after a legal cutoff.

candidates.title: Fair retry scheduling
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python scheduler for failed jobs. Repeated failures should delay a job more, one noisy job must not prevent ready jobs from running, equal-priority ready jobs must have deterministic order, and callers must be able to inspect why the next job is or is not ready. Use a supplied clock and only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: per-job next-ready timestamps in a stable priority queue
candidates.admission_rationale: Specifies delay, fairness, determinism, and explanations without naming the scheduling data structure.
candidates.human_analogy: Patients receive return appointment cards; the waiting room calls the earliest due card, breaking simultaneous appointments by printed patient number.

candidates.title: Capability-compatible plugin selection
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python selector for plugins that declare provided capabilities, required host capabilities, a priority, and a stable name. Return the best compatible plugin and an explanation for every rejection. Adding an unrelated capability must not alter the result. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: set containment filter then stable lexicographic ranking
candidates.admission_rationale: States compatibility and stability requirements without prescribing representation or selection pipeline.
candidates.human_analogy: Electrical adapters are first screened by plug and voltage compatibility; only among safe adapters does the traveler choose by preference and name.

candidates.title: Desired-state reconciliation
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python planner that compares desired named resources with observed resources and emits create, update, and delete operations. Applying its operations to the observed snapshot must produce the desired snapshot; planning again after application must emit no operations. Ordering must be deterministic and destructive operations identifiable before execution. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: pure canonical state diff with convergent operation ordering
candidates.admission_rationale: Defines convergence and audit behavior but does not name the pure diff organization.
candidates.human_analogy: A stage manager compares the final cast list with people currently on stage and writes entrances, costume changes, and exits; replaying the list leaves no further notes.

candidates.title: Historical account reconstruction
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python account history that accepts timestamped credits and debits, answers balance at any past sequence position, rejects overspending according to the state at insertion, and can verify that a supplied snapshot agrees with its history. Existing history must never be rewritten. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: append-only events reduced into state with verifiable snapshots
candidates.admission_rationale: The no-rewrite requirement is a constraint, while the event/reduction organization and snapshot role remain withheld.
candidates.human_analogy: Tree rings are never edited; current size is reconstructed by accumulating rings, and a claimed age marker is checked against the ring sequence.

candidates.title: Bounded batch execution report
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python batch runner for named callables with a maximum concurrency. Every submitted item must yield exactly one result record in input order, including failures and cancellations, and one failure must not erase other outcomes. The report must summarize success without inspecting exception text. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: indexed result envelopes with bounded worker pool
candidates.admission_rationale: States output algebra and bound without prescribing execution or result representation.
candidates.human_analogy: A school trip clipboard has one numbered row per child; every row ends as arrived, absent, or diverted, regardless of the order buses report.

candidates.title: Chunk-independent record decoder
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python decoder for length-prefixed UTF-8 records received in arbitrary byte chunks. It must emit each complete record exactly once, retain incomplete input, reject oversized records before buffering their full body, and produce the same records for every chunking of the same bytes. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: incremental parser with explicit header/body phases
candidates.admission_rationale: Specifies wire format and chunk invariance but withholds the phase organization.
candidates.human_analogy: A warehouse clerk first reads a package label’s promised size, then fills exactly that bin across deliveries before opening the next label.

candidates.title: Nested reversible edits
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python key-value workspace supporting begin, set, delete, commit, and rollback, including nesting. Rolling back an inner scope restores exactly the outer view; committing an inner scope keeps its changes subject to outer rollback. Reads must be efficient enough not to copy the whole workspace on every operation. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: stack of overlay journals with tombstones
candidates.admission_rationale: Defines nested semantics and rules out naive full copies but leaves the representation and merge behavior unstated.
candidates.human_analogy: Transparent drafting sheets stack over a base drawing; removing a sheet reveals the prior view, while accepting a sheet inks it onto the sheet below.

candidates.title: Stable continuation through changing data
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python paginator over records with creation time and unique id. A continuation value must let a caller resume without duplicates, and inserts newer than the first page must not shift already reachable records. Ties in creation time must be stable, continuation values must be opaque to callers, and malformed values rejected. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: keyset continuation over a frozen compound boundary
candidates.admission_rationale: States continuation invariants without identifying the comparison key or encoding strategy.
candidates.human_analogy: A reader resumes from a bookmark naming the last line and edition, rather than recounting pages after new preface pages are inserted.

candidates.title: Order-preserving update compaction
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python compactor for a sequence of key updates and deletions. Output the smallest sequence with the same final mapping, preserve the relative order in which surviving keys last became final, retain deletions only when requested, and never mutate input records. Use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: reverse scan selecting final occurrence then stable reversal
candidates.admission_rationale: Defines semantic equivalence, minimality, and order but withholds the one-pass organization.
candidates.human_analogy: Editing a meeting transcript from the end: keep only each speaker’s final correction, then restore the surviving notes to chronological order.

candidates.title: Repeated alert suppression
candidates.requirement: Implement a Python alert filter that emits the first occurrence of an alert identity, suppresses repeats for a configurable interval, reports how many were suppressed with the next emitted alert, and bounds memory when identities disappear. Behavior must be deterministic under a supplied clock and use only the standard library.
candidates.hidden_structure: per-identity expiring aggregation records with lazy eviction
candidates.admission_rationale: Specifies temporal behavior and boundedness without naming the stored record or cleanup strategy.
candidates.human_analogy: A receptionist keeps one message slip per caller for a short shift, adding tally marks for repeats, then hands over the tally on the next accepted call.
